conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure while maintaining a small allocation.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and cure the mandate breach.

balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a reasonable growth outlook.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL, targeting 6% each, to increase leveraged ETF exposure.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretched growth. It utilizes and adds to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, and CRWD to zero, eliminating all leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30% of the book, to prioritize income and covered-call ETFs.
Trim SPY to 20% and QQQ to 10% to reduce concentration and maintain a broad index base.

This plan focuses on generating steady monthly distributions with low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, aiming to park cash for yield. It rotates into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index, cutting leverage and high-beta names. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff. This is cash-like income, not a savings account.
